deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. This page is a worked example ('Eine Anwendung vorstehender Formeln') of the formulas on folio 7. Those formulas give the first-order effect of refraction and parallax on right ascension and declination. The task is to reduce the geocentric (Connaissance des tems) place of the Sun to its apparent topocentric place at Göttingen, 1809 May 11, at clock readings 0h35m0s and 1h15m0s.

FORMULAS USED (from f.7). Notation: φ = latitude, h = hour angle, δ = declination, ϱ = refraction at 45° altitude (so that the refraction is ϱ·tan z), π = horizontal parallax (so that the parallax is π·sin z).
- Auxiliary angle: tan θ = tan φ / cos h.
- Using cos z = sinφ sinδ + cosφ cosδ cos h = cosφ cos h cos(θ−δ)/cos θ, the refraction terms become:
  - Δα_refr = ϱ cosθ tan h /(cosδ cos(θ−δ))
  - Δδ_refr = ϱ tan(θ−δ)
- The parallax terms become:
  - Δα_par = −π cosφ sin h / cosδ
  - Δδ_par = −π sinφ sin(θ−δ)/sin θ
  - The last uses cosφ cos h / cos θ = sinφ / sin θ.

STEP 1: clock time to true time.
- The clock read 3h2m21.2s at true Göttingen noon on May 10 and 3h6m11.7s on May 11. So 24h of true solar time corresponds to 24h3m50.5s on the clock.
- [My inference: this is a sidereal clock about 6 s/day slow, since its reading at noon ≈ the Sun's RA.]
- Case I: clock interval since noon May 10 = 24h35m0 − 3h2m21.2 = 21h32m38.8 = 77558.8 s. True time = 77558.8 × 86400/86630.5 = 77352.4 s = 21h29m12.4s (astronomical time, May 10; i.e. about 9h29m a.m. civil, May 11).
- Case II: 79958.8 s → 79746.05 s = 22h9m6.0s.
- Paris true time = Göttingen − 30m21.0s, giving 20h58m51.4 and 21h38m45.0.
- For these instants the Connaissance des tems gives:
  - I: α = 3h10m58.61s, δ = 17°48′37.2″
  - II: α = 3h11m5.11s, δ = 17°49′2.9″
- Plausibility of these values: hourly rates of about 9.8 s in α and about 38″ in δ fit mid-May.

STEP 2: constants.
- log ϱ: mean value 1.7649 (58.2″) times barometer/thermometer factor 9.9684−10 (×0.930) gives log ϱ = 1.7333 (ϱ = 54.1″).
- log π: mean solar parallax log 0.9345 (8.6″) minus log(Sun–Earth distance) 0.0047 (r ≈ 1.011) gives log π = 0.9298 (π = 8.51″).
- φ (Göttingen) enters through log tan φ = 0.09988, log sin φ = 9.89374, log cos φ = 9.79385 (φ ≈ 51°31.8′).

STEP 3: hour angle.
- The Sun's hour angle equals true solar time.
- I: h = 21h29m12.4s = −37°41′54″ = 322°18′6″.
- II: h = 332°16′15″ as written.

STEP 4: auxiliary angle.
- I: log tan θ = 0.09988 − (9.89831−10) = 0.20157, so θ = 57°50′58″ and θ−δ = 40°2′21″.
- II: log tan θ = 0.09988 + 0.05298 = 0.15286, so θ = 54°53′16″ and θ−δ = 37°4′13″.

STEP 5: logarithmic sums ('n' marks a negative factor; C.log = cologarithm).
- RA refraction, log ϱ + log cosθ + log tan h + C log cosδ + C log cos(θ−δ):
  - I: 1.48474n → −30.5″
  - II: 1.33319n → −21.5″
- Dec refraction, log ϱ + log tan(θ−δ):
  - I: 1.65772 → +45.5″
  - II: 1.61152 → +40.9″
- RA parallax, log π(n) + log cosφ + log sin h(n) + C log cosδ:
  - I: 0.53138 → +3.4″
  - II: 0.41271 → +2.6″
- Dec parallax, log π(n) + log sinφ + log sin(θ−δ) + C log sinθ:
  - I: 0.70425n → −5.1″
  - II: 0.69095n → −4.9″

STEP 6: results.
- α (in arc): 47°44′39.1″ and 47°46′16.6″.
- Apparent RA: 47°44′12.0″ and 47°45′57.7″.
- Apparent Dec: 17°49′17.6″ and 17°49′38.9″.

Physical sense of the signs: the morning Sun is east of the meridian (sin h < 0). Refraction lifts it toward the zenith, reducing |h|, so RA decreases; it also moves the Sun toward the pole-side zenith, so Dec increases. Parallax acts in the opposite direction, as computed.
errors: Hour angle II is inconsistent with the time in the table. The tabulated true time 22h9m6.0s, which I recompute from the clock data as 22h9m6.05s, implies h = 360° − 27°43′30″ = 332°16′30″. Gauss's 332°16′15″ (and his log cos h = 9.94702, log tan h = 9.72071n, log sin h = 9.66773n, all checked to agree with 27°43′45″) corresponds to 22h9m5.0s. The time entries 22h9m6,0 and Paris 21h38m45,0 are visibly overwritten, so the time was probably corrected from 5.0 to 6.0 after the trigonometric work was done.
The 15″ hour-angle discrepancy changes the corrections by well under 0.1″, so the final apparent places are unaffected at the precision kept.

All other entries were checked and are correct to the last decimal or within ±1 unit in the 5th logarithmic place: logarithms, θ, θ−δ, the four logarithmic sums, the antilogarithms (30.5, 21.5, 45.5, 40.9, 3.4, 2.6, 5.1, 4.9 arcsec), the RA conversions to arc, and the final sums.
The method is first-order and uses the simple refraction law ϱ·tan z with a single constant. This is adequate at z ≈ 50–55° but is an approximation, not an error.

results.what: First-order corrections for refraction (ϱ tan z) and parallax (π sin z) in right ascension and declination, put in logarithm-friendly form via the auxiliary angle tan θ = tan φ / cos h, and applied numerically to the Sun at Göttingen
results.modern_name: Reduction of geocentric to apparent topocentric equatorial coordinates (differential refraction and diurnal parallax in α, δ) with an auxiliary angle
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th/early-19th-century spherical astronomy (e.g. Lalande, Delambre, Bessel's tables); auxiliary-angle forms are textbook material

results.what: Conversion of clock time to true local time by linear interpolation of the clock correction between successive true noons, plus a longitude difference Göttingen–Paris of 30m21.0s
results.modern_name: Clock correction/rate interpolation; longitude reduction to the ephemeris meridian

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine worked example of standard spherical-astronomy reductions with seven-figure logarithms. Its only interest is documentary: it shows Gauss's 1809 working constants (log ϱ, solar parallax 8.6″, the Göttingen–Paris longitude 30m21s) and a small hour-angle/time inconsistency that suggests a later correction.

checkable.asserts: True time II ≈ 22.15168 h = 22h9m6.05s, so h should be 332°16′30″, not 332°16′15″

transcription_corrections: The doubtful '0,53138[?]' is 0,53138; it is confirmed by summing the column (0.92980+9.79385+9.78640+0.02133).
In the time table, '22h 9' 6,0' and Paris '21 38 45,0' are overwritten in the manuscript, probably corrected from 5,0 and 44,0.
In the first time row, '12"4' and Paris '51"4' are also overwritten.
'C. log cos θ−δ' means C.log cos(θ−δ). 'log tang θ−δ' means log tan(θ−δ); the word 'tang' is overwritten.
In the parallax-in-RA block, the multiplier 'log π 0,92980 n' carries the 'n' (negative) flag on both columns, as transcribed.
